title: The Amount a ShieldCare Plan Pays on an Approved Repair Claim
content:
## The quantity defined

Where a claim on a Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan stands approved for repair, the amount the plan pays
is defined from the entries the repairer has booked against the job on the covered item, held in the records
of Northbeam TechWorks Installation and Repair.

1. **The window read** is the last 12 months.
2. **The covered bill** is the labour, the parts and the attendance charges booked against the job on the
   covered item inside the window read, each met at the share the plan carries. The parts met are the most
   recent parts entry booked on the job, whenever it was booked. The plan meets 75 percent of the parts
   booked, 90 percent of the labour booked, and none of the attendance charges booked. The covered bill is
   the labour met, the parts met and the attendance met added together, the total taken to the cent.
3. The attendance charges are the trip charge, the after hours surcharge and the mileage beyond the covered
   radius booked on that job; a no-show fee, a reschedule fee, a cancellation fee, a haul-away fee and a
   diagnostic fee are not attendance charges and the plan meets none of them under this head.
4. **The cover left on the plan** is the cover credited to it, together with any cover put back at an
   anniversary, less the payouts already booked against it.
5. **The ceiling on the settlement** is the plan's per-claim limit or the cover left on the plan, whichever
   is the lower.
6. **The room the plan's aggregate cap leaves** is that cap less the payouts booked on the plan in the
   rolling 12 months ending on the day of settlement, and never below nothing.
7. **The amount the plan pays** is the covered bill or that ceiling, whichever is the lower, and is then cut
   back to the room the plan's aggregate cap leaves for the rolling 12 months, taken to the cent. The
   cut-back to that room is made after the per-claim limit and the cover left, and never before them.

The plan meets nothing of a job the repairer has booked as work the manufacturer's warranty on the covered
item was still running to meet, and the entries the plan meets are read from the repairer's own ledger on
that job.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

The job on the covered item carries labour of 200.00 booked in the window read, a most recent parts entry of
150.00, and an after hours surcharge of 80.00. The plan's per-claim limit is 1600.00; the cover credited is
4000.00 with 3000.00 of payouts already booked; its aggregate cap is 5000.00 with 800.00 of payouts in the
rolling 12 months.

| Component | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| labour met, at 90 percent of 200.00 | 180.00 |
| parts met, at 75 percent of the 150.00 most recent parts entry | 112.50 |
| attendance met, none of the 80.00 booked | 0.00 |
| the covered bill, the three added together and taken to the cent | 292.50 |
| the cover left on the plan | 1000.00 |
| the ceiling on the settlement, the lower of 1600.00 and 1000.00 | 1000.00 |
| the room the aggregate cap leaves | 4200.00 |
| the amount the plan pays | 292.50 |

Had a haul-away fee of 45.00 stood on the same job, it would not enter the covered bill at all, because a
haul-away fee is not an attendance charge. Had the cover left stood at 200.00 instead, the ceiling would be
200.00, the lower of the covered bill and the ceiling would be 200.00, and the room the cap leaves would not
bring that down further, so the plan would pay 200.00 and the customer would carry the rest.
